7203.full: εὔ-θυμος, -ον [in LXX: 2Ma.11:26 * ;] __1. kind (Hom.). __2. of good cheer (Æsch., al.): Act.27:36.† (AS)

7204.full: 1. of persons, easily satisfied, contented with one's food , [variant datesAnthology Palantina, (Plutarch) 2. easily satisfied, contented, good-natured, peaceable , Lat. facilis, comis, (Aristophanes Comicus); with dative, εὔκολος πολίταις friendly to them, at peace with them, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;adverb -λως, tranquilly, calmly , (Plato Philosophus) 3. willing, agile , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 4. in bad sense, easily led, prone , πρὸς ἀδικίαν (Lucian) 5. of things, easy , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

7210.lxx: in LXX for כֶּסֶא, Psa.81:3 (-ως, from LXX 219)*
7210.full: εὔσημος, -ον (εὖ + οῆμα, a sign) [in LXX for כֶּסֶא, Psa.81:3 (-ως, from LXX 219)* ;] __1. conspicuous (cf. Ps, l.with). __2. clear to the understanding, distinct: 1Co.14:9.† (AS)

7212.full: εὔσπλαγχνος, -ον (εὖ, σπλάγχνον, which see), [in Man.1.7 (Camb. Manual LXX, iii, 825) ;] __1. in Hippocr., as medical term (LS, see word). __2. Metaphorical (cf. εὐσιλαγχνία, Eurip., Rhes., 192), in NT, tenderhearted, compassionate: Eph.4:32, 1Pe.3:8.† (AS)

7219.full: 1. full of life, lively , Lat. vivax, (Plato Philosophus):—;adverb, ζωτικῶς ἔχειν to be fond of life , (Plutarch) 2. of works of Art, true to life , τὸ ζωτικὸν φαίνεσθαι πῶς ἐνεργάζῃ τοῖς ἀνδριᾶσι; how do you produce that look of life in your statues? (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

7225.lxx: in LXX for חַי (chiefly) and cognate forms; frequently in Wis
7225.full: ζῷον (Rec. ζῶον, see LS, see word), -ου, τό (ζωός, alive), [in LXX for חַי (chiefly) and cognate forms; frequently in Wis ;] a living creature, an animal: Rev.4:6-9 5:6 ff. Rev.6:1 ff. Rev.7:11 14:3 15:7 19:4; ζῴων τ. αἷμα, Heb.13:11; ἄλογα ζ., 2Pe.2:12, Ju 10.† SYN.: θηρίον, in which the brutal, bestial element is emphasized, and which is never used of sacrificial animals. On the other hand, ζ. is the more comprehensive, as expressing the vital element common to the whole anima] creation (see Tr., Syn., LXXxi; Cremer, 274). (AS)

7238.full: θειότης, -ητος, ἡ (θεῖος) [in LXX: Wis.18:9 * ;] divine nature, divinity: Rom.1:20 (for ex. from π., see MM, Exp., xv).† SYN.: θεότης, deity, godhead, divine personality. θει. = divine nature and properties, a summary term for the attributes of deity, differing from θεότης as quality or attribute from essence (AS)

7242.lxx: in LXX: Dan LXX Bel 1:32, Th Bel 1:33*
7242.full: θεριστής, -οῦ, ὁ (θερίζω), [in LXX: Dan LXX Bel 1:32, Th Bel 1:33* ;] a reaper: Mat.13:30, 39† (AS)

7253.full: θιγγάνω [in LXX for נָגַע, Exo.19:12 * ;] __1. to touch, handle: Col.2:21, Heb.12:20" (LXX) . __2. to injure (like Heb. נָגַע, and as in Eur., Iph. Aul., 1351): with genitive, Heb.11:28.† SYN.: see: ἅπτω (AS)

7255.full: 1. muddy, foul, thick, troubled , Lat. turbidus, properly of water, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. metaphorically troubled by passion or madness , θολεροὶ λόγοι (Aeschulus Tragicus); θολερῷ χειμῶνι with turbid storm of madness, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

s: to be troubled, as by an alarm
7260.full: θροέω, -ῶ (θρόος, a noise, tumult), [in LXX: Sng.5:4 (הָמָה * ;] in cl., __1. to cry aloud, make an outcry. __2. to utter aloud. __3. In NT (and LXX), pass., to be troubled, as by an alarm: Mat.24:6, Mrk.13:7, Luk.24:37 (WH, mg.), 2Th.2:2 (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 126).† (AS)

7264.full: suiting the heart , i. e. well-pleasing, dear, delightful , (Homer):—;neuter as adverb in the form θυμῆρες, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

7267.full: an African tree with scented wood , a kind of juniper or cedar , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

7274.full: θέλησις, -εως, ἡ (θέλω) [in LXX: 2Ch.15:15, Pro.8:35 (רָצוֹן), Eze.18:23 (חֵפֶץ), LXX Dan.11:45 (צְבִי), Tob.12:18, Wis.16:25, 2Ma.12:16, 3Ma.2:26 * ;] in colloq. and MGr. = τὸ θέλειν, will: Heb.2:4.† (AS)

7275.lxx: in LXX: Job.6:17, Psa.19:6, Ecc.4:11 (חָמַם and derivatives), Sir.38:28 *
7275.full: θέρμη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: Job.6:17, Psa.19:6, Ecc.4:11 (חָמַם and derivatives), Sir.38:28 * ;] heat: Act.28:3.† (AS)

s: company marching through the streets with dance and song
in honour of Bacchus, a band of revellers
7276.full: 1. a band or company marching through the streets with dance and song , especially in honour of Bacchus, a band of revellers , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. generally, any party, company, troop , (Euripides) (ML)

7277.full: 1. a bag, pouch, wallet , (Herdotus Historicus); δερῶ σε θύλακον I'll make a bag of your skin, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. in plural the trousers of the Persians, (Euripides) (ML)

7289.full: καθαρότης, -ητος, ἡ (καθαρός), [in LXX: Exo.24:10 (טֹהַר), Wis.7:24 * ;] purity, cleanness: with genitive, Heb.9:13.† (AS)

7295.full: to be fast asleep, fall asleep , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., perfect participle κατυπνωμένος asleep , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

7298.full: καθ-άπτω [in Sm.: Sng.1:6 * ;] __1. to fasten on, put upon, with accusative __2. Act. for mid. (cf. Bl., § 53, 3), to lay hold of, attack: with genitive, χειρός, Act.28:3.† (AS)
